what         a cut of those files, every line verbatim: the genes TP53, GAPDH (human), Trp53, Gapdh (mouse)
             and Tp53 (rat); their gene-tree rows; and the two Compara alignments (gene trees
             ENSGT00950000183153 and ENSGT00940000153298) that hold human TP53's and GAPDH's canonical
             proteins, with the rows of the five canonical proteins and one zebrafish row each
why cut      the alignment is 908 MB; mzLib's own test for #1465 (Test/FileReadingTests/
             TestComparaGeneTreeAlignment.cs at cc67b7a29) writes a made-up alignment at run time and
             ships none
script       make_inputs.py (this folder): python make_inputs.py <folder of the release-116 files> <folder>
             (what is kept, and why each column number is still the release's own, is in its docstring)
checked      the queries of genes_map_residues_tp53.json, run by the bridge on the FULL release-116
             files (all three GTFs, the whole gene-tree file and the whole alignment), gave the same
             nine rows, column numbers included; that run kept 64,114 proteins from 54,308 alignments
             and took 55 s
determinism  gzip with mtime 0, no file name in the header, level 9; two runs gave identical sha256s
